**DynaLM 0.5.0.** One command, `dynalm cpu-report`, measures DynaLM against llama.cpp on any CPU and writes a report to share. The engine's speed and defaults are the same as in 0.4.0.

## New: `dynalm cpu-report`

Run it on your machine and attach the two files it writes to [issue #31](https://github.com/dynalm-project/dynalm/issues/31). The results tell us where DynaLM's CPU kernels need work on CPUs other than the Apple M4.

```sh
dynalm cpu-report --dry-run   # what it would run on this CPU, nothing downloaded
dynalm cpu-report --quick     # Qwen2.5-1.5B only, one round, about 15-20 minutes
dynalm cpu-report             # Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, two rounds, about 1-2 hours
```

- **Detects the CPU itself.** It reads the CPU's features (for example NEON, dot-product, i8mm, SME, AVX2, AVX-VNNI, AVX-512, AMX) and picks what to measure from them:
  - DynaLM's default;
  - the other kernel family (ggml's or DynaLM's own);
  - each further DynaLM kernel tier the CPU has;
  - llama.cpp's `llama-server`, with the same model file, threads and client.
- **Three model sizes:** Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B (Q4_K_M). A model that needs more RAM than the machine has is skipped, and the report says so (8B needs 12 GB).
- **Accuracy check:** on the 1.5B model, every DynaLM path is scored against llama.cpp on the same wikitext-2 tokens. A path passes with top-1 agreement of at least 94% and a perplexity at most 1% above llama.cpp's.
- **Speed:** 512-token prompts, 128 output tokens, 1 and 4 users. It reports tokens per second, the ratio to llama.cpp, time to first token, and the time between tokens (p50 and p99).
- **Detailed progress.** Seven numbered steps, every line stamped with the time since the start:
  1. what it detected about the machine;
  2. what it plans to run;
  3. llama.cpp;
  4. power and load;
  5. the models;
  6. each accuracy score;
  7. each speed run.

  Each server writes a log file, and the progress names it when something fails.
- **Honest numbers:** a run on battery or on a busy machine is marked **uncontrolled** in the report.
- **Verified downloads:** the models, a pinned llama.cpp release (b11695, about 15 MB) and wikitext-2 (5 MB) are each checked against their SHA-256. `--llama DIR` uses your own llama.cpp build instead.
- **Privacy:** prompts and outputs are not stored. `--anonymous` keeps the host name out of the report.

Details: [docs/cli.md](https://github.com/dynalm-project/dynalm/blob/v0.5.0/docs/cli.md#dynalm-cpu-report-measure-dynalm-against-llamacpp-on-this-cpu).

## Documentation

[docs/perf/cpu-experiments.md](https://github.com/dynalm-project/dynalm/blob/v0.5.0/docs/perf/cpu-experiments.md): on an Apple M4 Pro, decoding is measurably slower for about 110 ms after a prompt processed with SME. This explains why DynaLM's p99 time between tokens is higher than llama.cpp's at one user, while its overall throughput is higher.

## Supported environment

As in 0.4.0:
- **Verified:** macOS on Apple Silicon (one Apple M4 Pro).
- **CI-tested:** the Linux, Windows and macOS Intel builds are built and tested in CI, without real models. `cpu-report` has run end to end only on the Apple M4 Pro so far; reports from other CPUs are what this release asks for.
- **Experimental:** Vulkan and CUDA.
- **CPU path:** the fast path needs SME (Apple M4 class); other CPUs run ggml's CPU kernels by default.

## Upgrade

Replace the binary, or run the install script again. Nothing existing was changed or removed.
